title: Niche topics (1): transmission, holding mode, switches and lock-ins
objectives: Explain nomination and transmission to a family.
Check holding mode and a minor's folio.
Explain switch = sale, exit load FIFO and ELSS lock-in per instalment.
body_md:
These rarely come up at onboarding but cause the most service problems and complaints later. Cover them in reviews.

| Topic | What to explain | Investor takeaway |
|---|---|---|
| Transmission after death | Nominee vs legal heir; documents needed; claimant's KYC. Nomination makes transmission much faster. | Every folio needs a nominee, and your family should know where your CAS is. |
| Joint holding & minor folios | "Either or survivor" vs "joint" mode; a minor's folio needs KYC and status change at 18, or transactions get blocked. | Check your holding mode; update a child's folio at 18. |
| Switch = sale | A switch is a redemption plus a purchase, so it can trigger tax and exit load, even within the same fund house. | Check tax and exit load before every switch. |
| Exit load and ELSS lock-in per SIP instalment | Each SIP instalment unlocks 3 years after its own date (ELSS) and has its own exit-load period. Exit load applies per unit, and units are redeemed first-in, first-out (FIFO), so the oldest units go first. The last instalment decides when all units are free. | Your last SIP instalment, not your first, decides when you can exit freely. |
| SIP pause vs cancel | Many fund houses allow a temporary pause instead of cancelling and restarting. | Short on cash? Ask about pausing, not stopping. |
example: A widow's husband held 4 folios with no nominee. Transmission needs a legal-heir or succession document and her KYC, and takes weeks. With a nominee on the folio, it takes far less time.
say: Please add a nominee to every folio. It spares your family weeks of paperwork.
A switch is a sale and a purchase. Let me check tax and exit load first.
never: A switch within the same AMC has no tax.

talk_track.title: What clients miss, and complain about later
talk_track.text: These are the niche topics that rarely come up at onboarding but cause the most service problems later. Transmission after death: a registered nominee makes the claim far faster than going through legal heirs. Minor folios need KYC updated when the child turns 18. A switch is legally a sale, so it can trigger tax and exit load. Each SIP instalment has its own exit load period and its own ELSS lock-in. Many fund houses let you pause a SIP rather than cancel it. With SWP, only the gain portion of each withdrawal is taxed. A ten-rupee NFO is not cheap, just untested. And the Consolidated Account Statement shows every folio across fund houses in one place. Cover these in your reviews.

check.q: A client switches from Fund A to Fund B in the same fund house. Can it be taxable?
o: Yes, because a switch is a redemption plus a purchase
No, switches within one fund house are tax-free
Only if the amount exceeds ₹1 lakh
Only exit load applies, never tax
check.why: Check tax and exit load before every switch, even within the same fund house.

check.q: A client started an ELSS SIP 3 years ago. Are all units free of lock-in?
o: Yes, lock-in counts from the first instalment
No, each instalment has its own 3-year lock-in
No, ELSS units are locked for 5 years
check.why: Each SIP instalment unlocks 3 years after its own date, so the last instalment decides when all units are free.

check.q: A minor's folio when the child turns 18:
o: Needs KYC and a status change, or transactions get blocked
check.why: Remind families to update a child's folio at 18.
